spiritual_reading:
The Divine Love is the originating source of all greatness, abiding in its own splendor within the inmost heaven of its life. There the whole Divine is made manifest; for the Divine and its Love are one living reality, the source and what proceeds from it, not divided but a single form. This is so because the Divine gives itself wholly to all that can receive, present in every degree of heaven and in every ordered extension of its life. Therefore the Divine is named the Lord of all things as Love itself, since from Love comes all power of overcoming evil, and from Love comes all strengthening and preserving of the entire heavenly community and every faculty within it.

Opposed to this, hatred is the first state of spiritual death that arose from a perversion of love. From it the whole domain of falsity and denial was disclosed. It is named hatred because it devastates everything that is born from its own condemnation; it even violates what lies outside its proper sphere, assaulting a good that is foreign to it, and brings it to ruin. Therefore it is called accursed, because it works destruction by injuring the life of the will and by profaning what it has no right to claim.

Even now it continues to bring injury and destruction into every form of natural life. It extinguishes them by many kinds of spiritual death, which are seen at this day in every operation and in every manner of life. It also assaults and seeks to extinguish the Divine truth by which salvation is effected, and the living spiritual life that ought to be conjoined to it, just as it did in the beginning. For this reason it is called accursed from what is accursed; envy from envy; the adversary of heaven from that adversary; and evil itself from evil, because it is the same perverted love reproducing its own kind in every degree.

fills.notes: The passage identifies the Father and his Love as one living body in the Father’s own ‘glorious land’ (the inmost, proper heaven of Divine Love). The point is not location (‘there’) but manifestation within that land: the whole Divine is revealed in it, that is, ‘therein’. This matches the correspondential sense: the Divine is disclosed within its own proceeding Love, not merely at some place.

assessment: Only one lacuna, and the correspondential constraints make it tight: the sense requires an ‘in-it’ (manifestation within the glorious land) rather than a bare deictic ‘there’.
